title: GigaEvo: An Open Source Optimization Framework Powered By LLMs And Evolution Algorithms

mechanism.domainTask: Open-source LLM-guided optimization framework for mathematical and algorithmic discovery
mechanism.populationDetail: The framework supports multiple independent MAP-Elites islands with periodic migration, although all reported experiments use a single-island setup.
mechanism.archiveDetail: MAP-Elites maps programs into behavior-space cells (fitness and validity, or alternative dimensions) and preserves the best occupant in each cell.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Redis persists program records and lineage, but the evolutionary archive updates cell incumbents by within-cell fitness comparison; lineage persistence is not a tree population.
mechanism.generationDetail: The mutation operator conditions on one selected parent program and emits either a diff or a complete rewrite explicitly prompted to localize changes.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Validity, complexity, objective metrics, and execution exceptions are stored as structured metadata; insights and lineage descriptions are generated textual feedback.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Elites are sampled by fitness-proportional selection from the active MAP-Elites archive; multi-island mode scopes the pool to an island, while single-island experiments use one archive. Exact number of selected parent programs is not specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Bidirectional ancestor-and-descendant lineage analysis is assembled into mutation context, allowing guidance from both prior and later descendants; this lineage-guided framework capability is not fully captured by current contextual-reference labels.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/GIGAEVO An Open Source Optimization Framework Powered by LLMs and Evolution Algorithms.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey placements for localized modification and score-based parent selection are supported. Multi-island is a framework capability while all reported experiments are single-island; model assignments vary across tasks, and the explicit small/large exploration-refinement schedule is bin-packing-specific. MAP-Elites uses descriptors but retains scalar fitness as the primary objective.
